title: Mock Test Analysis Methodology
tagline: Year 4 — Turning a mock test into a diagnosis: sectional accuracy, time per question, error types and an improvement plan

introduction.overview: A mock test is useful only if you analyse it. The analysis has four parts: scores and accuracy by section, time per question by section, a classification of every wrong or skipped question (could not do, careless, ran out of time, misread, guessed), and a specific plan for the next week. This chapter works through the arithmetic of the analysis on an illustrative mock. The figures in this chapter's examples are illustrative and not real test statistics.
introduction.placementRelevance: Candidates who analyse every mock improve faster than those who take more mocks without analysis.
introduction.realWorldContext: Post-mortems and retrospectives are the standard way teams learn.

learningObjectives: Identify the biggest loss of marks
Write a specific plan for the next mock

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Accuracy = correct ÷ attempted. Time per question = time ÷ attempted. Marks lost = wrong × penalty + missed.

coreDefinitions: Careless error: an error you could have avoided.
Skipped-but-solvable: a skip you could have solved in time.
Plan: a specific action for the next week.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Analysis turns a score into causes, and causes into actions.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Fill a table: attempts, correct, time per section; tag each wrong answer; pick the biggest cause.

mainNarrative: Illustrative mock: Aptitude 20 questions in 25 minutes: attempted 18, correct 14, wrong 4. Accuracy 14 ÷ 18 = 77.8%; time per attempted question 1,500 ÷ 18 = 83 s; net marks (penalty 0.25) = 14 − 1 = 13.
Reasoning 15 in 20 minutes: attempted 12, correct 9: accuracy 75%.
Verbal 25 in 20 minutes: attempted 25, correct 15: accuracy 60%, time per question 48 s.
Classify the 12 wrong answers: 5 careless, 3 misread, 2 guessed, 2 could not do: careless errors are the largest cause.
Plan: add a 10-second check for units and last digit; practise reading stems twice; take one timed verbal drill daily.

deepDiveAspects.content: A wrong answer loses marks plus the penalty; a skipped question loses only the opportunity.
